Research/Paper: Toward Generating a New Dataset for Intrusion Detection and Intrusion Prevention: CIC-IDS2017 (Sharafaldin et al.)
Problem Addressed: Lack of realistic, modern benign and malicious network flow datasets with full packet features.
Method: Extracted 79 flow statistical features from simulated testbed pcap captures (DoS, PortScan, Infiltration, Web Attacks).
Limitation: High class imbalance; statistical features lack explicit host topology and business service criticality mappings.
Relevance to SafeContain AI: SafeContain AI incorporates the CIC-IDS2017 PortScan dataset via a dedicated adapter (cic_ids_adapter.py) to benchmark intrusion flow ingestion.

Research/Paper: From Local Explanations to Global Understanding with Explainable AI (Lundberg et al.)
Problem Addressed: Opaque black-box ML model predictions in critical decision domains without verifiable feature attribution.
Method: Game-theoretic Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) with exact closed-form solutions for linear models.
Limitation: High computational complexity for deep non-linear networks; assumes feature independence in standard formulations.
Relevance to SafeContain AI: Directly utilized in SafeContain AI (explainability.py) via SHAP LinearExplainer to provide SecOps analysts with verifiable risk drivers.

Research/Paper: Automated Cyber Defense Containment Optimization Using Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (Alserhani et al.)
Problem Addressed: Unconstrained automated containment disrupts critical enterprise operations, causing unacceptable business outages.
Method: Formulated 0-1 Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) to select defense actions minimizing security risk under cost constraints.
Limitation: Failed to model dynamic business workflow SLA downtime constraints or verify containment actions in sandbox snapshots before execution.
Relevance to SafeContain AI: Foundational inspiration for SafeContain AI’s Google OR-Tools CP-SAT optimizer, which extends MILP with Business Continuity Twin SLA bounds.

Research/Paper: Blockchain-Based Immutable Audit Logs for Security Operations Centers (Al-Daeef et al.)
Problem Addressed: Vulnerability of centralized SOC audit trails to insider tampering, log deletion, and retroactive forensic manipulation.
Method: Cryptographic hash chaining coupled with decentralized public/consortium blockchain smart contract anchoring.
Limitation: High public blockchain gas costs and latency when anchoring individual high-velocity telemetry logs on-chain.
Relevance to SafeContain AI: Directly solved by SafeContain AI (merkle.py, blockchain_client.py) using binary Merkle trees: batches 1,000s of events into single 32-byte roots.

Research/Paper: A Survey on Cybersecurity Digital Twins for Critical Infrastructure (Bhamare et al.)
Problem Addressed: Lack of safe environments to test security responses without taking live production systems offline.
Method: Digital Twin modeling mirroring physical network topologies, operational states, and industrial protocols.
Limitation: Primarily focused on SCADA/ICS hardware rather than enterprise financial workflows and SaaS business continuity.
Relevance to SafeContain AI: SafeContain AI adapts the Digital Twin concept (twin.py, sandbox.py) into an enterprise Business Continuity Twin evaluating $/hr downtime loss.

Research/Paper: Managing Attack Graph Complexity Through Metric-Driven Topological Aggregation (Noel & Jajodia)
Problem Addressed: Combinatorial explosion of multi-hop attack paths in large enterprise networks overwhelming security analysts.
Method: Graph metrics, subnet aggregation, and reachability reduction to condense complex exploit graphs into manageable routes.
Limitation: Static graph models that do not dynamically sync with live graph databases or update with streaming telemetry.
Relevance to SafeContain AI: Directly applied in SafeContain AI (engine.py) via NetworkX dual-engine Dijkstra reachability and Neo4j parameterized Cypher MERGE synchronizer.

Research/Paper: Attack Graph Analysis and Automated Response Selection in Cyber-Physical Systems (Kotenko & Chechulin)
Problem Addressed: Manual response selection is too slow against automated multi-stage lateral intrusions.
Method: Graph-based response catalog generation evaluated against multi-objective heuristic scoring functions.
Limitation: Heuristic scoring lacks mathematical optimality guarantees compared to exact discrete solvers (CP-SAT/ILP).
Relevance to SafeContain AI: Benchmarked in SafeContain AI (comparator.py): compares Kotenko-style Greedy heuristics directly against exact OR-Tools CP-SAT optimization.

Research/Paper: Temporal Cyber Risk Forecasting Using Hidden Markov Models and Graph Neural Networks (Zheng et al.)
Problem Addressed: Reactive security tools only identify attacks after compromise has already occurred; lack forward-looking threat horizons.
Method: Integrated multi-state Markov transitions and graph convolutions to project temporal intrusion trajectories across 6h-24h horizons.
Limitation: High training compute overhead and limited operational interpretability for Tier 1 SOC triage analysts.
Relevance to SafeContain AI: Implemented in SafeContain AI (forecasting/engine.py, early_warning/engine.py) to forecast forward risk trajectories and pre-attack clusters.
